It differs from general AMR structures by enforcing a strict preorder traversal ID scheme and storing four vertex-centered scalars per element to avoid runtime index lookups, building on the [TET-AMR Data Structure](1094-tet-amr-data-structure.md) layout [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the structure enforces a strict preorder traversal ID scheme. Source [S1] Section 3.2.3 explicitly states: 'reordering the elements so that every element will have all its descendants before the next sibling element of the parent; this corresponds to elements being given IDs ordered according to the preorder traversal'. Source [S1] Section 3.2.4 states: 'duplicate the vertex-centered data and store four vertex-centered scalars per element. This confirms the storage method and the reason (avoiding the indexing array/runtime lookups). The claim mentions building on the TET-AMR Data Structure layout, which is the context of the provided source [S1] titled 'TET-AMR Data Structure'. All facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
